study type: Retrospective review of routine health facility data
exposure: Availability and design of 21 maternal and newborn health (MNH) data elements in routine labour and delivery ward registers
outcome: Availability of routine labour and delivery ward register data
Quality of routine labour and delivery ward register data (completeness, implausibility, internal consistency, heaping)
Utility of routine labour and delivery ward register data for calculating MNH indicators
cohort: The study participants were 20,075 births recorded in routine labour and delivery ward registers from five public hospitals in Bangladesh, Nepal, and Tanzania over a one-year period (2016-17).
finding: Data required to calculate maternal and newborn health indicators were largely available and highly complete in routine labour ward registers across the study hospitals, though register designs need to be improved for intervention coverage measurement and data quality can be strengthened.
birth_weight: Birthweight data quality (completeness, heaping) was assessed, revealing less completeness for stillbirths and significant heaping, especially at 2500g and 3000g.
